Roro/container: build the port, broker and currency decision file

Before the final commercial comparison, create a 'what could reverse the decision? ' note for this RoRo versus container shipping transaction. Use route availability, vehicle operability/dimensions, loading/securing, damage exposure, insurance, destination handling, timing and final delivery as the comparison backbone and then apply the Latin America operating questions: port choice, currency basis, customs/clearing handoff, inland distance, energy/fuel fit, parts and workshop access. Identify which unknowns would merely change convenience and which could change legality, use, landed cost or support. Only the second group belongs in the payment stop list. Keep the first group visible but do not let it force artificial completeness. This materiality test keeps the method useful across countries while ensuring the actual destination receives the deeper verification it needs.

Ask what each document actually proves. The preferred evidence for this decision is current forwarder/carrier or port-route evidence plus written loading, insurance and handoff responsibilities. A manufacturer source can establish its named market; a seller document can establish the offer; a destination authority or local operator can establish its own requirement. Do not let one layer impersonate another. When two sources disagree, resolve the scope or keep the point open instead of choosing the more convenient answer.

Obtain separate, dated confirmation of terminal handling, storage and onward transport charges. Where a charge remains unknown, show it as an open item rather than substituting a regional average.

Frequently asked questions

What must be fixed before requesting a quote? — RoRo versus container vehicle shipping

Fix the destination, importer, exact vehicle version, quantity, operating task, route and evidence date. A quote without those boundaries cannot be compared reliably. Keep original files and written answers so another reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.

Which evidence is not sufficient on its own? — RoRo versus container vehicle shipping

A brochure, seller screenshot, isolated photograph, regional model name or verbal assurance is not enough. Match independent and official evidence to the same vehicle and destination. Use the final authority and delivered version; names used in advertising do not establish compliance.

When should the buyer run a sample? — RoRo versus container vehicle shipping

Run a sample whenever registration, loading, climate, road duty, diagnostics or after-sales support has not already been demonstrated for the exact version and route. Separate confirmed, excluded and unknown costs, and assign every unknown an owner and deadline.

Which findings should stop payment or shipment? — RoRo versus container vehicle shipping

Stop when identifiers conflict, approval scope is uncertain, documents cannot be traced, material costs are omitted or the responsible party refuses a dated written answer. Make the sample follow the same documents, route and operating task intended for the batch.
